10: # Post-install event data
11: 
12: > Pass post-install event data from your app to Unity Ads through an MMP to optimize user acquisition campaigns based on real user engagement, such as sessions, purchases, ad revenue, and level completions.
13: 
14: Unity Ads User Acquisition campaigns that are optimized for acquiring particular kinds of users, such as [Retention](/grow/acquire/campaigns/retention/retention-campaigns.md), [Return on Ad Spend](/grow/acquire/campaigns/roas/return-on-ad-spend-campaigns.md) (ROAS), and [Event](/grow/acquire/campaigns/event/event-campaigns.md) campaigns, require information about how users engage with your app after installing it. Post-install event data informs Unity's models to more accurately show ads to your campaign's target audience.
15: 
16: When you integrate with an MMP, you can enable your preferred partner to pass post-install event data to Unity. Each type of optimized campaign requires at least one type of post-install event data. However, you can pass data from all event types to any of your campaigns. The recommended best practice is to pass data for all post-install events because the additional data can improve your campaign performance.
17: 
18: Integrated partners can pass the following types of post-install event data:
19: 
20: | Post-install event | Description                                                           | Related campaigns                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
21: | ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
22: | Session            | Users open your app                                                   | [Retention](/grow/acquire/campaigns/retention/retention-campaigns.md)                                                                                                                                                              |
23: | Purchase           | Purchases users make in your app                                      | * [In-app Purchase (IAP) ROAS](/grow/acquire/campaigns/roas/purchase/in-app-purchase.md)
24: * [Hybrid ROAS](/grow/acquire/campaigns/roas/hybrid/hybrid.md)
25: * [Payer](/grow/acquire/campaigns/event/intro-to-event-campaigns.md#payer) |
26: | Ad revenue         | Revenue from ads that your users watch in your app                    | - [Ad Revenue ROAS](/grow/acquire/campaigns/roas/ad-revenue/ad-revenue.md)
27: - [Hybrid ROAS](/grow/acquire/campaigns/roas/hybrid/hybrid.md)                                                                                          |
28: | Level Complete     | A specific milestone or completion event your users reach in your app | [Level Complete](/grow/acquire/campaigns/event/intro-to-event-campaigns.md#level-complete)                                                                                                                                         |

20: This topic explains how budget settings dictate how much marketing spend your user acquisition campaigns could consume.
21: 
22: > **Important:**
23: >
24: > Campaign budget limits are estimates. Because actual spend depends on many factors including campaign performance, Unity does not guarantee that you will be invoiced according to the budget limit amount.
25: 
26: ## Organization budgets##organiza
27: 
28: The overall marketing budget your organization has available to spend with Unity's ad platform is called an Organization budget. If the organization budget reaches zero, all activity with the organization's ad campaigns will pause until there is an available organization budget to spend from.
29: 
30: Your active ad campaigns consume your organization budget. To limit how much of your organization budget an individual campaign can spend, you can set two kinds of campaign-level budgets:
31: 
32: * **Campaign budget**: the overall budget for an individual campaign
33: * **Daily budget**: the target spending for a single day in an individual campaign
34: 
35: Both the campaign budget and the daily budget are optional campaign settings. If you leave these budget settings empty, the campaign will spend an unlimited amount until the organization budget is consumed or the campaign ends.
36: 
37: > **Note:**
38: >
39: > Use the [Reporting dashboard](/grow/acquire/reporting/dashboard/reporting-dashboard.md) or the [Advertiser Statistics API](/grow/acquire/reporting/api-reports.md) to understand how your organization consumes its budget.
40: 
41: ### Budget remaining##budget
42: 
43: You can view the balance of your organization budget in the bottom of the Unity Ads User Acquisition dashboard secondary navigation menu. You can also select **Budget remaining** > **Add funds** to make payments to your organization budget. For more information, refer to the [Budgets and payments](/grow/acquire/budgets.md) documentation.
44: 
45: > **Note:**
46: >
47: > If you have set up post payments with a client partner, the **Budget remaining** section will display **Credit line in use** instead of a balance amount. Refer to the [Post payments](/grow/acquire/budgets/payments/introduction.md#post) documentation for more information.
48: 
49: ## Campaign budgets##campaign
50: 
51: Campaign budgets determine how much of your organization budget can be consumed by an individual campaign. Campaign budgets are optional; if you do not set a campaign budget, your campaign will spend an unlimited amount of your overall organization budget.
52: 
53: ## Daily budget##daily
54: 
55: Use Daily budgets to set a target for how much of the campaign budget you would like the campaign to spend each day. Think of the daily budget as an average daily spend of your campaign budget. The Unity User Acquisition system will use the target budget to throttle your campaign as you reach the limit.
56: 
57: However, successful campaigns with low budgets might occasionally overspend the daily budget. Daily budgets reset at midnight, UTC. When you set a daily budget, you can choose between a campaign-level budget or country-level budgets. Country-level budgets can be individual or grouped:
58: 
59: * **Campaign-level daily budget**: A single daily limit that applies across all countries.
60: * **Per-country daily budget**: Individual daily limits for each targeted country.
61: * **Multi-country daily budget**: A shared daily budget pooled across a group of countries, with Unity's algorithm automatically distributing spend within the group based on performance.

63: ### Multi-country daily budgets
64: 
65: Multi-country daily budgets allow you to share a campaign's daily spending limit across multiple grouped budgets. Each budget group can contain multiple countries. You define groups of countries and set one shared budget per group. Unity's optimization system then distributes spend across the countries in each group in real time, prioritizing where bids win and conversions happen.
66: 
67: > **Tip:**
68: >
69: > Multi-country budgets work simultaneously with per-country daily budgets in the same campaign.
70: 
71: Country group daily budgets are available for all campaign types. For guidance on when to use them and how to structure your groups, refer to [Budget best practices](/grow/acquire/budgets/best-practices.md). For setup instructions, refer to [Set daily budgets](/grow/acquire/budgets/set-daily-budget.md).
72: 
73: ### Daily Cap status
74: 
75: The Daily Cap is a set of campaign statuses that notify you when a live campaign has already spent its daily budget. Campaigns with the Daily Capped and Geo Capped statuses are not currently spending, even though they are set as live.
76: 
77: > **Note:**
78: >
79: > Daily Cap statuses are only visible for live campaigns. For more information, review the documentation on how to [set campaigns live](/grow/acquire/campaigns/set-campaigns-live.md).
80: 
81: The following table details the Daily Cap statuses and their corresponding [daily budgets](/grow/acquire/budgets/set-daily-budget.md):
82: 
83: | **Status**   | **Daily budget** | **Description**                                                                                                                          |
84: | ------------ | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
85: | Daily Capped | All countries    | The campaign is live but is unable to deliver ads because it has met its daily budget.                                                   |
86: | Geo Capped   | Per country      | The campaign is live but is unable to deliver ads (or is partially delivering ads) because one or more country has met its daily budget. |

14: ## Optimize budgets
15: 
16: Automated bidding is one option for controlling your daily campaign spend. Automated bidding dynamically adjusts your bids throughout the day to optimize how your budget is used. You can use both CPM and CPI billing with Automated bidding.
17: 
18: When you use cost per install (CPI) billing without Automated bidding, successful campaigns will occasionally spend their campaign budget too quickly when they have several successful days in one week. Automated bidding can help you maintain budget limits on a weekly basis. If your campaign overspends one day, Automated bidding adjusts your budget for the next day to compensate. This ensures your campaign stays within budget on a weekly basis.
19: 
20: When you set your daily budget with Automated bidding, aim for one-seventh of the amount you want your campaign to spend in a week. Use this calculation for both CPI-billed and CPM-billed campaigns.
21: 
22: Automated bidding also optimizes your bids so your budget is used more efficiently. By adjusting your bids based on campaign performance, Automated bidding maximizes the number of installs your campaign can achieve in a day.
23: 
24: ### Optimize budgets with ROAS campaigns
25: 
26: ROAS (return on ad spend) campaigns also benefit from Automated bidding. When you run a ROAS campaign, with CPI billing, the campaign automatically uses Automated bidding. This bidding strategy helps improve campaign performance for campaigns that are constrained by their daily cap. By optimizing how your bids are placed, using CPI billing in these campaigns can increase your observed return on ad spend (ROAS).
27: 
28: For more information about [Automated bids](/grow/acquire/bids.md), refer to the Bids documentation.
29: 
30: > **Important:**
31: >
32: > Changing your budget might have an impact on how accurately the daily budget can be respected on a weekly basis. If you change your budget mid-campaign, it will take approximately seven days for the system to accurately respect the new budget on a weekly basis.

34: ## Recommendations and strategy
35: 
36: When you start adding budgets to your campaign, Unity offers recommendations for your minimum campaign budget and minimum daily budget. These recommendations are based on the billing type, the number of creatives assigned, and the countries the campaign is targeting.
37: 
38: Before the Unity algorithm can deliver your first campaign results, it needs to explore your campaign and creatives. To ensure that the algorithm has sufficient funds for the exploration process, set a campaign budget that's at least five times the value of your daily budget.
39: 
40: For campaigns billed on impressions (CPM), Unity recommends you start with the minimum budget recommendations offered in the dashboard. These recommendations are designed to mitigate the risk of overspending during the exploration phase with [tCPI bidding](/grow/acquire/bids.md). After the exploration phase, you can increase or remove the daily budget limit to enable higher impression volumes.

73: > **Tip:**
74: >
75: > The recommended best practice is to group countries with similar advertising costs (CPI) or revenue potential (ARPU or ROAS).
76: 
77: For a focused budget strategy with more pacing control, keep high-priority markets (for example, the US) in individual country groups with a per-country budget.
78: 
79: ### Set daily budgets based on weekly targets
80: 
81: Unity's budget management operates on a 7-day rolling window rather than enforcing hard daily limits. Daily spend varies slightly from day to day within that window. If your campaign overspends on one day, spend will be lower on subsequent days to compensate, and vice versa. Over a full week, the average daily spend will meet your goal.
82: 
83: This behavior applies to all daily budget types, including country group daily budgets. Set your daily budget based on your weekly target divided by seven for the most predictable results.

16: ## Prerequisites
17: 
18: Before you set up your ROAS campaign, ensure that your [organization budget](/grow/acquire/budgets/set-organization-budget.md) has funds.
19: 
20: ## Create a ROAS campaign in the User Acquisition Dashboard
21: 
22: To create a new ROAS campaign, complete the following steps:
23: 
24: 1. From the **Apps** page of the User Acquisition Dashboard, select your app to open the **Campaigns** list for your selected app.
25: 2. On the **Campaigns** page, select **Create** to enter the campaign creation flow.
26: 3. Select **Return on Ad Spend** as your campaign goal.
27: 4. In the **ROAS-specific settings**, choose your optimization type from the following options:
28:    * **In-app purchases**: Target users predicted to make in-app purchases.
29:    * **Ad revenue**: Target users predicted to engage with in-app ads.
30:    * **Hybrid**: Target users predicted to both make purchases and engage with ads in your app.
31: 5. Select the **Optimization Window** for your campaign. Refer to the [Introduction to ROAS campaigns](/grow/acquire/campaigns/roas/intro-to-roas-campaigns.md#optimization-windows) for details on which optimization types support which windows.
32: 6. Name your campaign and select **Create**.
33: 7. To launch your campaign and start the [Learning phase](/grow/acquire/campaigns/roas/intro-to-roas-campaigns.md#learning-phase), configure the following required settings:
34: 
35:    * Add at least one [creative pack](/grow/acquire/creatives.md).
36:    * Choose which countries to target and set a [ROAS goal](/grow/acquire/campaigns/roas/intro-to-roas-campaigns.md#roas-goals) for each.
37:    * Set a [campaign budget](/grow/acquire/budgets/introduction.md#campaign).
38:    * Add [attribution](/grow/acquire/partner-integration/attribution/attribution-links.md) links.
39: 
40:    > **Note:**
41:    >
42:    > Each optimization type has required post-install events. The dashboard lists the required event type in the **Attribution** setup section.

13: Auction dynamics
14: The MAX In-App Bidding Exchange is a first-price, fair and transparent, unified first-price auction in which the highest bidder wins.
15: All SDK in-app bidders and DSPs have equal access to each ad impression opportunity.
16: They receive full notification coverage with enhanced macros.
17: The MAX In-App Bidding Exchange collects bids for individual impression opportunities from SDK-based demand partners and DSPs.
18: It does this via the OpenRTB 2.5 protocol.
19: To integrate with MAX, a bidder must comply with the OpenRTB 2.5 API.
20: To read the MAX in-app bidding spec for SDK-based in-app bidders, see
21: the AppLovin oRTB specification page
22: MAX ad serving flow
23: The user launches the app.
24: MAX initializes all eligible SDKs.
25: The publisher requests an ad.
26: For SDK bidders, MAX collects bid tokens from initialized SDKs.
27: MAX SDK makes an ad request to MAX ad server.
28: MAX auction server requests bids from eligible SDK bidder endpoints and DSPs in AppLovin Exchange.
29: It passes identity tokens in the bid request to SDK bidders.
30: DSPs and SDK bidders return real-time bids in the maximum timeout threshold (
31: tmax
32: ).
33: MAX auction server merges these with the non-bidding demand sources in the publisher waterfall.
34: MAX auction server resolves the auction based on the highest CPM value.
35: MAX sends loss notifications to bidders that lose the auction due to error or invalid bid (e.g. below the floor, missing bid value, zero as bid price).
36: If the winner is a DSP, MAX notifies the DSP and the AppLovin SDK loads and shows the ad.
37: If the winner is an SDK bidder, MAX notifies the winning demand partner’s SDK so that it can load and show the ad.
38: If the load succeeds, MAX sends a win notification to the bidder.
39: If the load does not succeed, MAX sends a loss notification to the bidder.
40: After the ad renders, MAX calls the winner’s billing URL.

20: ### Overview
21: 
22: A publishing app submits an ad request to Unity's exchange, where DSPs can submit a bid for the impression. If the bid wins the auction, Unity pre-caches the ad and only renders it when the user views the ad. At this point, an impression and all other trackers are counted.
23: 
24: 1. Unity receives an ad request from a mobile device.
25: 2. Unity makes an HTTP POST [request](/grow/programmatic/unity-exchange/bid-requests.md) to all bidding partner endpoints.
26: 3. For waterfall auctions, TMAX is configurable by the DSP seat, up to 1000ms. For bidding auctions, TMAX is configured by the mediation platform; 50ms is deducted from Unity's processing time. In both scenarios, the DSP's time to respond is communicated in the bid request.
27: 4. Unity's Exchange runs a first-price auction based on valid bidder responses.
28: 5. Upon completing the auction, Unity retrieves the winning bid's HTML and impression trackers to the client for pre-caching.
29: 6. When the player experiences the ad, Unity pings the winning bidder's `nURL` to notify the DSP of the impression.
30: 7. The creative renders to the end user, and Unity fires other event trackers along with the creative payload.
31: 
32: > **Note:**
33: >
34: > When supported, if a bid loses the auction, Unity sends [loss reason codes](/grow/programmatic/unity-exchange/loss-notifications.md) to the bidder.
